newsitem.title: UK: Abbey, Hambros in private bank deal.
newsitem.headline: Abbey, Hambros in private bank deal.

text.p: British bank Abbey National Plc, best known for its mortgage lending, and investment bank Hambros Plc said on Wednesday they will enter a private banking joint venture with Hong Kong bank Dah Sing.
Abbey and Hambros will each contribute HK$85 million (some 6.6 million pounds) to have 49 percent of the capital but will control only 19.8 percent of the voting rights.

The venture is intended to exploit the massive growth in the Far East private banking market -- the region is set to overtake Europe and North Amrica as the biggest private banking market in the world.
The partners said they expect to attract clients in Hong Kong and other parts of South East Asia with liquid assets in excess of $250,000 and will set up an offshore bank in Guernsey.
The British partners feel that having a Hong Kong bank at the head of the venture will give them an edge over other prospective entrants into what is a highly competitive market.
Abbey currently has no private banking exposure as such while Hambros does manage money for some individuals but does not class this activity as one of its core businesses.

"This new venture gives us the opportunity to develop a core business for Hambros in what we believe to be one of the fastest growing private banking markets in the world," said Hambros chief executive Charles Perrin.
Abbey, which does have an expanding offshore business in Jersey, said the venture will help it build this aspect of its business.
Dah Sing is a medium-sized player in the Hong Kong market which reported net profits of HK$477 million in 1995 and had total assets of HK$33 billion at the end of last year.
